key_insight: A stacked machine-learning pipeline and neural network were used to detect early Alzheimer’s disease and highlight important biomarkers from clinical, cognitive, and neuroimaging-related data.
clinical_relevance: Earlier identification of likely Alzheimer’s cases could support timelier clinical evaluation and care planning before symptoms become severe.
method: ADNI data were cleaned with iterative imputation for missing values.
Class imbalance was addressed with Borderline SVM-SMOTE, followed by feature selection and scaling.
A stacking ensemble (Logistic Regression, Extra Trees, Bagging KNN, LightGBM) was compared with an artificial neural network.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on ADNI data using precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC to compare model performance.
watch_item: Results may depend on ADNI-specific data quality and class balancing choices, so external validation is needed before broader use.
paper_title: Predicting Early Stages Of Alzheimer's Disease And Identifying Key Biomarkers Using Deep Artificial Neural Network And Ensemble Of Machine Learning Methodologies
